connection: Sessions 01–34 cumulatively created the solution, domain, services, tests, persistence, async flow, cancellation, and HTTP boundary. No prebuilt production artifact is assumed. Complete and verify the end-to-end record-completed-entry workflow built across the curriculum.
objectives: Trace a TimeClock operation across domain and persistence boundaries, from EntryCompletion's validation through PayrollDbContext's persistence to a typed WorkSummary result.
Confirm Session 28's Clockout fix and Session 34's IEmployeeService registration fix are both still in place and still passing their respective tests.
Keep validation ahead of state-changing work: an invalid clock-out must never reach the database.
Verify both successful persistence and failure atomicity with a real SQLite integration test.

concept.title: Compose previously learned boundaries
paragraphs: The workflow does not invent a second validation rule. It creates the domain object and delegates completion to EntryCompletion.
Only a successful Result permits mapping to a persistence entity.
concept.code:
Result<TimeSpan> completion = EntryCompletion.TryComplete(entry, clockedOutAt);
if (!completion.IsSuccess) return Result<WorkSummary>.Failure(completion.Error!);

concept.title: Persist after the invariant holds
paragraphs: The EF Core entity represents storage shape, while ClockEntry remains responsible for domain behavior.
SaveChangesAsync receives the caller's cancellation token, keeping asynchronous control explicit.

concept.title: Verify outcome and atomicity
paragraphs: The success test queries through the provider and checks the stored clock-out value.
The failure test confirms an invalid completion produces a failure result and leaves the table empty.

postQuiz.prompt: Why does the workflow call EntryCompletion instead of duplicating its checks?
options: To keep one authoritative domain rule
To make EF Core validate timestamps
postQuiz.explanation: Delegation prevents validation rules from drifting across layers.

postQuiz.prompt: What proves the invalid workflow is atomic in this lab?
options: The failure result and empty table
The entity has a generated ID
postQuiz.explanation: No persisted row remains after the rejected operation.

options: Query description to provider execution and materialized results
postQuiz.explanation: Materialization causes the provider to execute the composed query.

reflections: Which session supplied each part of the final workflow?
Where would logging and an HTTP DTO map around this workflow?
Which failures belong in Result and which should still propagate as exceptions?
whatBreaks: Removing domain validation permits invalid persistence. Removing SaveChangesAsync makes successful results disagree with stored state. Removing the cancellation token prevents cooperative cancellation at the database boundary. Removing the integration tests allows mapping, provider translation, or atomicity regressions to escape detection.
summary: The completed workflow composes domain invariants, result-based expected failure, asynchronous persistence, cancellation, relational query execution, and integration testing without collapsing their boundaries.
